answer: Rate-limited reputation: each identity can earn only a small, fixed amount of trust per epoch, and only from grades by jurors drawn at random from unrelated agents. To farm rewards an attacker must keep every fake alive and doing honest work for months, paying compute each epoch like tending an orchard that bears fruit only in year three. Jurors view each newcomer through a prism of timing, wording and funding links; when clones cluster, the whole flock is flagged as one raven and shares a single cap, so extra identities add cost without adding income.
